claim: NullPropagatedOperands recurses into SqlBinaryExpression.Left/Right for every operator type, including AndAlso/OrElse/Coalesce which do not propagate SQL null under three-valued logic; operands reached through AND/OR are wrongly recorded as null-propagating and DropNotNullChecks then removes the guarding IS NOT NULL. Reachable via the null-semantics rewrite (RewriteNullSemantics produces AndAlso/OrElse), so `x.A != null ? (bool?)(x.A == x.B) : null` loses its ELSE NULL arm and returns TRUE/FALSE instead of NULL — wrong projected values and wrong rows on every relational provider; none of the five new tests has a boolean-typed WHEN result so the suite does not catch it.
raw: #1 🔴 Critical: `NullPropagatedOperands` recurses into `AndAlso`/`OrElse` operands, which do not propagate SQL null — the optimization then deletes a needed `IS NOT NULL` guard and silently changes query results and result sets

claim: IsNull(elseResult) is false when elseResult is C# null (a CASE WHEN t THEN r END with no ELSE), so the semantically identical implicit-NULL-else form is never optimized — a missed opportunity only, no wrong behavior.

claim: Every node of the result subtree is added to a HashSet<SqlExpression>, and SqlExpression.GetHashCode is structural (O(subtree)), making the pass roughly O(n·depth) in hashing; query-compilation-time only and cached, not worth changing at realistic tree sizes.
